```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Global companion to rain_vs_flow_report.Rmd (US counties). Reads the
# figures and tables of 04_global_figures.R and the US tables of
# 01_rain_vs_flow_figures.R; run 03_global_cell_stats.py (all bands) and
# 04_global_figures.R first. Every number in the text is computed from
# these tables.
#
# Inputs:  output/figures/hydro/rain_vs_flow_global/*.png
#          output/data/hydro/rain_vs_flow_global/{coverage,group_summary,
#            snow_summary}.csv
#          output/data/hydro/rain_vs_flow/{group_summary,
#            annual_correlation}.csv   (US counties)
# Output:  rain_vs_flow_global_report.html, next to this file. Figures are
#          embedded, so the file opens on its own in a browser.
# Dependencies: dplyr, readr, tidyr, knitr, rmarkdown (pandoc, no LaTeX)
#
# Render from this folder on Midway:
#   Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("rain_vs_flow_global_report.Rmd")'

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, out.width = "100%")

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
```

```{css, echo = FALSE}
/* Number figures and tables in order ("Figure 1.", "Table 1.") at the start
   of each caption. Figures are numbered through their captions, so every
   figure and table needs one. */
body { counter-reset: figure table; }
.figure .caption::before, figcaption::before {
  counter-increment: figure;
  content: "Figure " counter(figure) ". ";
}
table caption::before {
  counter-increment: table;
  content: "Table " counter(table) ". ";
}
.figure .caption::before, figcaption::before, table caption::before {
  color: #0b0b0b;
  font-weight: bold;
}
/* Light-green label for the figures and tables to show the PI. Wrap a
   chunk in ::: {.pi-highlight} ... ::: to highlight its label. */
.pi-highlight .caption::before, .pi-highlight figcaption::before, .pi-highlight caption::before {
  background-color: #d9f2d0;
  padding: 2px 6px;
}
```

```{r paths}
USER <- Sys.getenv("USER")
source("../../../../../0_utils/paths.R")

fig_dir <- file.path(DIR_FIGURE, "hydro", "rain_vs_flow_global")
table_dir <- file.path(DIR_REPO_RAINFALL_MORTALITY, "output", "data", "hydro", "rain_vs_flow_global")
us_table_dir <- file.path(DIR_REPO_RAINFALL_MORTALITY, "output", "data", "hydro", "rain_vs_flow")
```

```{r read-data}
coverage <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "coverage.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
world <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "group_summary.csv"), col_types = cols(group = "c"))
snow <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "snow_summary.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
us_groups <- read_csv(file.path(us_table_dir, "group_summary.csv"), col_types = cols(group = "c"))
us_annual <- read_csv(file.path(us_table_dir, "annual_correlation.csv"), col_types = cols(group = "c"))

# Format numbers for the text and tables
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  vapply(x, function(v) format(signif(v, digits), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE), "")
}
fmt_r <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
fmt_pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x)
fmt_n <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)

group_names <- c("1" = "Low", "2" = "Middle", "3" = "High", "all" = "All")

# Median box, by weighting ("pop", "area"), group ("1", "2", "3", "all") and column
world_value <- function(g, column, w = "pop") world[[column]][world$weights == w & world$group == g]

# Median US county, same groups: monthly correlation, drought and flood
us_value <- function(g, column) {
  if (column == "corr_month") {
    us_groups$corr_median[us_groups$group == g]
  } else {
    us_annual$median[us_annual$group == g & us_annual$measure == column]
  }
}

# Share of US counties whose flow peaks in a different month, and their
# median upstream ratio, by group
us_group_value <- function(g, column) us_groups[[column]][us_groups$group == g]

# Cuts between the thirds: the top of the low and middle groups
world_cuts <- c(world_value("1", "ratio_max"), world_value("2", "ratio_max"))
us_cuts <- us_groups$ratio_max[match(c("1", "2"), us_groups$group)]

# Snow-share groups of low-third boxes, population weights
snow_pop <- filter(snow, weights == "pop")
snow_value <- function(label, column) snow_pop[[column]][snow_pop$snow == label]
snowy_share <- with(snow_pop, sum(n_boxes[snow %in% c("10-30%", "Over 30%")]) / sum(n_boxes))

# Largest gap between the population- and land-area-weighted medians
weights_gap <- world %>%
  select(weights, group, corr_month, corr_drought, corr_flood) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("corr"), names_to = "measure") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = weights, values_from = value) %>%
  summarise(gap = max(abs(pop - area))) %>%
  pull(gap)
```

# Summary

As in the U.S., flow is the same as rainfall.
In the top third of boxes by upstream ratio (mean flow/mean rainfall),
it is different, and affects the flood measure (annual max) more
than the drought measure (annual mean).
Snow affects far more of the map than rivers do: across northern Eurasia
and Canada, the flow and rainfall flood measures barely move together.
From these figures, it looks like rainfall_flow captures upstream rainfall
from outside the box and the timing of snowmelt, as in the U.S.

::: {.pi-highlight}

```{r table-world}
world %>%
  filter(weights == "pop") %>%
  transmute(
    group,
    `Upstream-ratio third` = group_names[group],
    Boxes = fmt_n(n_boxes),
    `Share of people` = fmt_pct(pop_share),
    `Monthly: world` = fmt_r(corr_month),
    `Monthly: US` = fmt_r(sapply(group, us_value, column = "corr_month")),
    `Drought: world` = fmt_r(corr_drought),
    `Drought: US` = fmt_r(sapply(group, us_value, column = "corr_drought")),
    `Flood: world` = fmt_r(corr_flood),
    `Flood: US` = fmt_r(sapply(group, us_value, column = "corr_flood"))
  ) %>%
  select(-group) %>%
  kable(
    align = "lrrrrrrrr",
    caption = paste0(
      "Correlation of rainfall_flow with rainfall, median 0.5-degree box (world) and median county (US) ",
      "in each upstream-ratio tertile. Thirds: boxes or counties ranked by upstream ratio ",
      "(mean flow / mean rainfall) and split into tertiles. The world thirds split at ",
      fmt(world_cuts[1]), " and ", fmt(world_cuts[2]), ", the US thirds at ", fmt(us_cuts[1]),
      " and ", fmt(us_cuts[2]), ". The monthly columns are the correlation over each box's or ",
      "county's own months. The drought and flood columns are correlations over 1950-2025 of the ",
      "flow and rainfall drought measures (annual mean of the monthly values) and flood measures ",
      "(annual max: the biggest monthly value)."
    )
  )
```

:::

# The comparison

**Boxes.** A 0.5-degree box (5 x 5 ERA5-Land cells, roughly county-sized)
plays the role of a US county. Rainfall (`tp_total`) and `rainfall_flow` are
averaged over the box's cells with population weights (LandScan 2011), as for
counties. The drought and flood measures are the annual mean and annual max
of the box's monthly values, built the same way for both series.

**Sample.** The `r fmt_n(coverage$n_boxes_compared)` boxes with people, which
hold `r fmt_pct(coverage$pop_compared_share)` of the LandScan population
between 57S and 84N. Maps use population weights.

# Across geography

```{r fig-ratio, fig.cap = "Upstream ratio (mean rainfall_flow / mean rainfall), by 0.5-degree box."}
include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "G1_upstream_ratio.png"))
```

- **The upstream ratio traces the river network.** The large rivers stand
  out: the Amazon and Paraná, the Mississippi, the Nile, Niger and Congo, the
  Ganges, Indus, Mekong and Yangtze, and the Volga and the Siberian rivers.

::: {.pi-highlight}

```{r fig-drought-flood, fig.cap = "Correlation of the flow and rainfall drought measures (annual mean) and flood measures (annual max), by 0.5-degree box."}
include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "G2_drought_flood.png"))
```

:::

# Across time

```{r fig-shift, fig.cap = "Months from the rainfall peak month to the rainfall_flow peak month, by 0.5-degree box."}
include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "G3_peak_shift.png"))
```

- **Same peak month** across most of the tropics and subtropics (Africa,
  South and Southeast Asia, China, South America, Australia).
- **Flow peaks earlier** across northern Eurasia and southern Canada, which
  fits spring snowmelt.
- **Flow peaks later** in the US Pacific Northwest and the Chilean Andes,
  which fits winter snow that melts in late spring.

::: {.pi-highlight}

```{r table-snow}
snow_pop %>%
  transmute(
    `Snow share` = snow,
    Boxes = fmt_n(n_boxes),
    `Monthly flow vs. monthly rainfall` = fmt_r(corr_month),
    `Drought measure` = fmt_r(corr_drought),
    `Flood measure` = fmt_r(corr_flood),
    `Flow peaks in a different month` = fmt_pct(share_peak_shifted)
  ) %>%
  kable(
    align = "lrrrrr",
    caption = paste(
      "Correlation of rainfall_flow with rainfall, median low-third box (little upstream water)",
      "by snow share. Snow share: the share of 1950-2025 precipitation stored as snow before it",
      "reaches the flow input."
    )
  )
```

:::
